abstract.p: 2-Amino-6-anilino-purine derivatives of formula (I) in which R1 is -S(O)k-NR6R7 or-N(aryl lower alkyl) carbamoyl or -NH-S(O)i-R8 or -NH-C(O)-R9; 9 is 1-5; These compounds inhibit p34<cdc2>/cyclin B<cdc13> kinase and protein tyrosine kinase pp60<c-src> and can be used for treatment of hyperproliferative diseases, for example tumour diseases, and diseases which respond to inhibition of the activity of protein tyrosine kinase pp60<c-src>, in particular osteoporosis.

L'invention concerne des dérivés 2-amino-6-anilino-purine de formule (I), dans laquelle R1 représente S(O)k-NR6R7, ou N(aryle alkyle inférieur) carbamoyle, ou NH-S(O)i-R8, ou NH-C(O)-R9; et 9 varie entre 1 et 5. Ces composés, qui inhibent la p34<cdc2>/cycline B<cdc13> kinase et la protéine tyrosine kinase pp60<c-src>, peuvent être utilisés pour traiter les maladies hyperprolifératives, par exemple les affections tumorales et les maladies répondant à l'inhibition de l'activité de ladite protéine tyrosine kinase pp60<c-src>, en particulier l'ostéoporose.

All these functional groups should not be on the C atom from which the free valency comes, and they are preferably separated from this by 2 or even more C atoms. The hydrocarbyl radical can also carry free and functionally modified carboxyl groups, such as carboxyl groups present in salt form or esterified carboxyl groups, carbamoyl, ureido or guanidino groups which may or may not carry one or two hydrocarbon radicals, and cyano groups.

A particular etherified hydroxyl group is the grouping methylenedioxy or ethylenedioxy, the former as a rule bridging 2 adjacent C atoms, in particular in aryl radicals, and the latter being bonded to one and the same C atom and being regarded as a protective group for oxo.

The compounds of the formula I and their pharmaceutically acceptable salts inhibit the enzyme p34 cdc2/cyclin Bcdc13 kinase. In addition to other cdc2-related kinases, this kinase controls certain phases during cell division, in particular the transition from the Gt phase into the S phase, and in particular the transition from the G2 phase into the M phase.

The cycle of a eukaryotic cell comprises, in chronological sequence, the interphase and the M phase. The interphase is accompanied by an enlargement of the cell. It in turn comprises, in chronological sequence, the Gi phase, the S phase and the G2 phase. In the G phase (G = "gap", i.e. interspace), biosynthetic processes proceed in the cell. In the S phase (synthesis phase), the DNA replicates. The cell then enters the G2 phase, which ends with the start of mitosis.
The M phase in turn comprises, in chronological sequence, division of the cell nucleus (mitosis) and division of the cytoplasm (cytokinesis).
